title: Insalata Caprese
subtitle: Classic tomato, mozzarella, and basil
excerpt: A simple assembly of ripe tomatoes, fresh mozzarella, and basil leaves dressed with good olive oil and a splash of balsamic. This is a recipe where ingredient quality makes all the difference.
sourceNotes: Insalata caprese is said to have originated on the island of Capri in the early twentieth century. Its colours mirror the Italian flag and it became a symbol of southern Italian summer eating. The recipe has no fixed proportions; adjust to what looks best on the plate.

recipe.makeAheadNotes: Slice the tomatoes and mozzarella up to 30 minutes ahead but do not dress until ready to serve.

content.text: Both the tomatoes and the mozzarella should be at room temperature. Cold mozzarella straight from the fridge is rubbery and flavourless. Take it out at least 30 minutes before you plan to serve. Use the ripest, most flavourful tomatoes you can find.

items.prepNote: ripe, ideally a mix of sizes, at room temperature
fresh buffalo mozzarella, at room temperature, drained

content.text: Slice the tomatoes into rounds about 1cm thick. Tear or slice the mozzarella to roughly the same thickness.
Arrange the tomato and mozzarella slices alternately on a serving plate, overlapping slightly. Tuck the basil leaves in between the slices.
Drizzle generously with olive oil and add the balsamic if using. Season with flaky sea salt and black pepper.
Serve immediately at room temperature. Do not refrigerate once dressed.

items.cause: It was served cold from the fridge.
items.fix: Rest mozzarella at room temperature for at least 30 minutes.

items.symptom: Tomatoes are releasing a lot of water.
items.cause: They were sliced too long before serving or over-salted.
items.fix: Dress just before serving; salt only at the very last moment.
